exchanges.question: How does Lilly envision expanding its increasingly deep consumer-facing position in obesity and where is the consumer market heading; how unique or similar is the U.S. self-pay market versus the international self-pay market?
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: U.S. and global obesity treatment is still only mid-single-digit utilization, so significant patient opportunity remains; access is improving with the Bridge program and state Medicaid coverage going live or committed for next year; Q2 obesity TRx reached about 3 million, driven by injectable and oral new patients, with about 55% of ZEPBOUND prescriptions self-pay; Lilly is investing in consumer awareness and expanding LillyDirect. Patrik: obesity outside the U.S. is still mainly out of pocket; Lilly is rapidly replicating U.S. consumer-activation practices and has launched versions of LillyDirect OUS, with models varying by local regulation and a common focus on patients receiving safe, authentic Lilly medicines.

exchanges.question: The U.S. Foundayo launch curve has been slower than anticipated: what are the contributing factors and when should an inflection be expected? Ex-U.S., how are competitive dynamics and the launch trajectory shaping up now that Novo Nordisk is scaling its oral in the U.K., Germany and the UAE, where Novo claims 50% share within three weeks?
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Lilly is focused on three fronts (physician education, access and affordability, consumer awareness) and leading indicators are positive with week-to-week prescription growth; in the last 30 days CVS added Foundayo in June, Bridge launched July 1 and the full DTC campaign began; in the last week of July volume almost doubled versus a month earlier and about one in four new starts are on Foundayo, so an inflection is now visible and growth is expected over the coming quarters. Patrik: the UAE launch in early May started strongly, orals are expanding the market and most patients are incretin-naive and titrating up; Lilly's combined incretin share held steady despite a second oral entering; Mexico and Saudi Arabia launch next with most launches in 2027, with no gating from supply; the early data are noisy and often reflect sell-in with inventory build.

exchanges.question: What are the requirements and milestones ahead for retatrutide to be accepted under the BLA pathway given the dispute with the FDA, and will BLA classification be unique to retatrutide or apply to subsequent incretins?
exchanges.answer: Lilly's position is that retatrutide is a biologic under both the amino acid count rule and as analogous to a protein; the first court decision was mixed and litigation is active, but Lilly hopes to reach a conclusion with the FDA supporting a BLA. All clinical data needed for submission are in hand but more CMC data must be gathered; Lilly is in communication with the agency and will update investors on filing status, with submission expected by Q1 next year. He called it a super exciting data package with unprecedented efficacy and a large lead over any triple-acting competitor.

exchanges.question: What are the early learnings and surprises from the Medicare obesity (GLP-1 Bridge) rollout, and what does the initial ramp look like for orals versus injectables?
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Bridge expands access to about 35% more Americans; it is early but a pretty significant inflection point is visible, and Lilly is working closely with CMS to educate physicians, pharmacies and consumers on criteria and prior authorization, which is working well; LillyDirect has been enabled to fulfil Bridge prescriptions. Both ZEPBOUND and MOUNJARO have inflected over the last few weeks, partly from Bridge; around 80% of people getting treatment are on injectables, and approximately 60%-70% are new patients who did not previously have access.

exchanges.question: Does retatrutide need a commercial strategy to protect against the unapproved product apparently available today, or will formal approval solve that; and with its higher efficacy, are there additional indications beyond tirzepatide's base that retatrutide can address?
exchanges.answer: People are eagerly awaiting authentic retatrutide and Lilly fully expects them to vote with their feet for the guaranteed product once it is on the market. Transformative weight loss at the high dose opens additional opportunities: knee osteoarthritis pain was reduced by an unprecedented 75% in TRIUMPH-4 and TRIUMPH-1; a MASH/MASLD study is ongoing where the glucagon mechanism may offer unique advantages; several additional indications are being evaluated internally; a chronic lower back pain study reads out sometime next year. Retatrutide can work at the high end with bariatric-surgery-like weight loss and at the low end with a single titration step.

exchanges.question: What is the post-Verzenio strategy in breast cancer given the oral SERD and oral PI3K assets, and is an all-oral combination on the table?
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly Oncology and Head of Business Development
exchanges.answer: The three most important targets in breast cancer are the estrogen receptor, CDK4/6 and PI3 kinase alpha; Lilly believes it has the best medicine for each and plans to combine them all. INLURIYO's adjuvant EMBER-4 trial reads out next year, a major moment for that medicine. Lilly is on the precipice of starting the phase III program for tersolisib (PI3K inhibitor), initially combined with existing endocrine therapies and investigator's choice of CDK4/6 (largely Verzenio), and over time combined with INLURIYO as an all-oral combination across settings.

exchanges.question: Guidance seems to imply a second-half revenue deceleration versus Q2 despite the Medicare Bridge ramp and Foundayo commercial access coming online; is something being missed on price, or is the team being conservative?
exchanges.answer: The full-year guide was raised by $2.5 billion. Recent quarters including Q2 included one-off prior-period adjustments to U.S. rebate and discount estimates that are not expected to continue in the second half. The 2025 base period included the bolus of MOUNJARO launches in new OUS countries, which will not repeat, and future OUS growth is driven by penetration rather than new countries; in dollars rather than percentage, significant growth is still expected in the second half. Seasonality is also factored in: Europe in Q3 from vacation holidays and U.S. Type 2 diabetes in Q4.

exchanges.question: Which specific regions are driving the most OUS MOUNJARO growth, and what is Lilly seeing in India where generic semaglutide is launching amid reported capacity constraints?
exchanges.answer: MOUNJARO continues to perform very strongly more or less everywhere with market leadership across many markets; key drivers are China, where NRDL listing delivered category leadership after 16 months, plus Korea, the U.K., Mexico and Germany, with share in many markets similar to or above U.S. levels. In India and Brazil MOUNJARO TRx continued to grow after generic semaglutide launched, driven by superiority data as the first line of defense; in Canada tirzepatide TRx is growing at the same pace as the total market. Generic companies are showing significant supply constraints, which Lilly is monitoring closely.

exchanges.question: How extensive is the Foundayo sampling program and is it dampening the weekly IQVIA prescription data; is the U.S. prescriber base expanding and can that be quantified?
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Every promotional lever is active; sampling covers the first 30 days of the first dose, similar to a typical oral small molecule in retail, is extensive across the prescriber base and fully supplied. The prescriber count has grown from about 8,000 at the last earnings call to 36,000, with continued week-on-week progress in adoption, awareness and perception of the Foundayo profile; Lilly feels good about inflection ahead as access and consumer awareness increase.

exchanges.question: ZEPBOUND net price appears to be about $580 per prescription, well above the cash price; how sustainable is the medical-exception-driven delta now that CVS is back on formulary, and is this what drives the favourable rebate adjustments quarter after quarter?
exchanges.answer: ZEPBOUND pricing is transparent across channels: LillyDirect direct-to-patient from $299 to $449, the Bridge program at $245, and the commercial price. Medical exceptions are one driver, and script size in the commercial segment is another, so price per pack is significantly lower than the per-prescription figure. After CVS moved to a one-of-one formulary last year patients had three options (switch to the competitor, go to the cash market, or use the medical exception process); CVS access resumes starting in Q4, medical exceptions are maybe a short-term thing and the goal is open access. Price is expected to go down for sure as a result, which is embedded in the guide and will be more than offset by volume growth.

exchanges.question: Lilly surprised investors by getting back into psychiatry and doing vaccine deals: are these areas Lilly can scale and a high priority, or are the assets more one-off and science-driven?
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly Oncology and Head of Business Development
exchanges.answer: What the two areas share is immense remaining unmet need, which is the through line of all internal and business development work; Lilly acquired technology and medicines it believes can be really impactful at prices that keep it disciplined and create long-term shareholder value, not unlike the other deals done year to date. He would not forward-look on whether Lilly builds further in infectious disease and psychiatry specifically, saying it will be opportunistic based on what is available, but is very excited about both areas and the assets purchased.

exchanges.question: Which one or two non-obesity pipeline assets is management most excited about that the street should be paying more attention to?
exchanges.answer: Cardiovascular: PCSK9 gene editing for ASCVD plus oral and injectable Lp(a)-lowering drugs, which are huge opportunities. Neuroscience: psychiatry, sleep-wake disorders via Centessa, and diseases like addiction and major depressive disorder that may be addressable with incretin science. Oncology: probably the richest readout period in Lilly's history, including Kelonia's in vivo CAR T for multiple myeloma and the AJ1-11095 JAK inhibitor. Immunology: still early days for the atopic dermatitis franchise (transcribed as empagliflozin) with new indications coming, plus combination ideas in IBD and psoriatic diseases; he called it the strongest pipeline Lilly has ever had, even excluding incretins.

exchanges.question: Foundayo sales of $31 million in the UAE alone were close to half the $67 million generated in the U.S., suggesting explosive ex-U.S. potential: how does Lilly see its ex-U.S. obesity potential, and will ex-U.S. governments reimburse Foundayo for diabetes better than tirzepatide given it can be offered much cheaper?
exchanges.answer: Lilly is encouraged by the UAE start but it is very early days with a lot of noise in the data and an initial inventory build alongside real demand; the learning so far is a clear need for an oral in both obesity and Type 2 diabetes, with the majority of patients incretin-naive. The major OUS rollout happens at the beginning of 2027. On Type 2 diabetes reimbursement, Lilly is probably slightly better positioned with an oral and three head-to-head orforglipron trials offering an appealing value proposition, but OUS reimbursement always takes time, so launch focus will be chronic weight management, building on U.S. and UAE experience.
